reply.english: Yesterday I went to the market.
I saw my aunt by chance.
Yes, I bought a new shirt.

phrases.arabic: أوَّلْ الْبَارِحْ كَانَتْ عِنْدِي الْخِدْمَة حْتَّى لِلعَشِيَّة

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: صباح الخير سلمى، كيفاش داز ليك البارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: sbaa7 l-khir Salma, keefaash daaz leek l-baare7?
dialogue.english: Good morning Salma, how was your yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله، كان نهار طويل بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: l-7amdulillah, kan nhar Tweel bzzaf.
dialogue.english: Thank God, it was a very long day.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: علاش؟ شنو درتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: 3laash? shnu derti?
dialogue.english: Why? What did you do?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: فقت معطلة، وخدمت حتى للعشية.
dialogue.transliteration: fqt m3aTTla, w khdemt 7ta l-l-3ashiya.
dialogue.english: I woke up late, and I worked until the evening.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وفالليل؟ فين كنتي؟
dialogue.transliteration: w f-l-leel? fin knti?
dialogue.english: And at night? Where were you?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: كلينا مع خواتي فمطعم زوين.
dialogue.transliteration: kleena m3a khwati f-maT3am zween.
dialogue.english: My sisters and I ate at a nice restaurant.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: زوين، شنو كليتو؟
dialogue.transliteration: zween, shnu kleetu?
dialogue.english: Nice, what did you eat?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: طاجين د الدجاج، وشربنا أتاي.
dialogue.transliteration: Taajeen d d-djaaj, w shrebna ataay.
dialogue.english: A chicken tagine, and we drank tea.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: وانت، شنو درتي أول البارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: w nta, shnu derti awwel l-baare7?
dialogue.english: And you, what did you do the day before yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: كانت عندي الخدمة حتى للعشية، وتعييت بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: kant 3endi l-khedma 7ta l-l-3ashiya, w t3ayit bzzaf.
dialogue.english: I had work until the evening and got very tired.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: الله يعاونك. واش شفتي شي واحد البارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: Allah y3awnek. waash shefti shi waa7ed l-baare7?
dialogue.english: May God help you. Did you see anyone yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: إيه، شفت كريم بالصدفة فالسوق.
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, sheft Kareem b-S-Sodfa f-s-souq.
dialogue.english: Yes, I saw Kareem by chance at the market.

pair.english: Where were you at seven in the evening?

response.arabic: لا، غير درت شوية د التقضية
response.transliteration: la, ghir dert shwiya d t-tqDiya
response.english: No, I only did a little shopping.

lessons.culture: البارح is the everyday word for yesterday and أول البارح the day before; the MSA أمس is not used in speech. شنو درتي؟ is a normal opener among friends and neighbours, and the form درتي is the same for a man and a woman.

exercises.prompt: صاحبك سولك: "البارح شنو درتي؟". جاوبو بلي مشيتي للسوق.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but too bookish for everyday Darija; مشيت للسوق البارح is what is said.

exercises.prompt: كيسولوك: "فين كنتي البارح فالليل؟". جاوب بلي كنتي فالدار.

too_formal.feedback: المنزل is written or formal; in speech people say الدار.

exercises.tip: "فالدار" = at home, the house being الدار.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "_____ كان نهار طويل بزاف." المعنى: Yesterday was a very long day.

too_formal.feedback: أمس is MSA; in Darija the word is البارح.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "تعييت بزاف من _____ البارح." المعنى: I got very tired from work yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: العمل is correct but bookish; Moroccans say الخدمة.

exercises.tip: "الخدمة" is the everyday word for work.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "What did you do yesterday?"

too_formal.feedback: ماذا is MSA; شنو is how "what" is said in Morocco.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who did you see yesterday?"

too_formal.feedback: من is MSA; شكون is the Moroccan "who".

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "I bought a new shirt yesterday"؟

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but the spoken forms are شريت and قميجة.

exercises.tip: "قميجة" is the Moroccan word for a shirt.

exercises.prompt: شنو معنى "حتى لأمتى بقيتي فايق البارح؟"؟
exercises.answer: How late did you stay up yesterday?
accepted: How late did you stay up yesterday?
options: How late did you stay up yesterday?

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: البارح الجو كان زوين بزاف
رتب الجملة: تعييت بزاف البارح من الخدمة

phrases.arabic: مْلِي كُنْتْ صْغِيرْ كُنْتْ كْنبْغِي نْلَعْبْ بْرَّا
phrases.transliteration: mli kunt Sgheer kunt kanbghi nl3eb brra

phrases.english: I grew up in an old neighborhood in Casablanca.

phrases.arabic: كُلْ صِيفْ كُنَّا كْنْمشِيو عِنْدْ جَدِّي فَالْبَادِيَة
phrases.transliteration: kol Seef kunna kanmshiw 3and jeddi f-l-baadiya

phrases.arabic: جَدِّتِي كَانَتْ كْتْحكِي لِينَا حْكَايَاتْ قْبَلْ مَا ننْعِسُّو
phrases.transliteration: jeddti kant kat7ki leena 7kaayaat qbel ma nn3essu

phrases.arabic: الْبِيسْكْلِيتْ لُولَة لِي كَانْ عِنْدِي كَانَتْ حمْرَا
مْلِي كُنْتْ صْغِيرْ كُنْتْ كْنْخَافْ بزَّافْ مِنْ الضَّلْمَة
phrases.transliteration: mli kunt Sgheer kunt kankhaaf bzzaf mn D-Dlma

phrases.arabic: الْمُعَلِّمْ دِيَالِي فَالْمدْرَسَة كَانْ حْنِينْ بزَّافْ
كُنَّا كْنْمشِيو لِلْمدْرَسَة مَعْ بَعْضِنَا كُلْ نْهَارْ
phrases.transliteration: kunna kanmshiw l-l-medrasa m3a b3Dna kol nhar

phrases.arabic: مْلِي كُنْتْ صْغِيرْ كُنْتْ كْنْحلِمْ نْوَلِّي طيَّارْ
phrases.transliteration: mli kunt Sgheer kunt kan7lem nwelli Tayyaar

phrases.arabic: فْدِيكْ السَّاعَة الدُّنْيَا كَانَتْ سَاهْلَة بزَّافْ
phrases.transliteration: f-deek s-saa3a d-dunya kant saahla bzzaf

dialogue.speaker: Kareem
dialogue.arabic: هند، واش فاكرة ملي كنا صغار؟
dialogue.transliteration: Hind, waash faakra mli kunna Sghaar?
dialogue.english: Hind, do you remember when we were small?

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: إيه، كنت كنبغي نلعب برا بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, kunt kanbghi nl3eb brra bzzaf.
dialogue.english: Yes, I loved to play outside a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Kareem
dialogue.arabic: وأنا كبرت فدرب قديم فالرباط.
dialogue.transliteration: w ana kbert f-derb qdeem f-r-rbaaT.
dialogue.english: And I grew up in an old neighbourhood in Rabat.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: وأنا فالدار البيضاء. كان عندي صاحبة سميتها ياسمين.
dialogue.transliteration: w ana f-d-daar l-beeDa. kan 3endi Saa7ba smiytha Yasmeen.
dialogue.english: And I in Casablanca. I had a friend called Yasmine.

dialogue.speaker: Kareem
dialogue.arabic: كنا كنلعبو الكورة فالدرب كل عشية.
dialogue.transliteration: kunna kanl3bu l-kura f-d-derb kol 3ashiya.
dialogue.english: We used to play football in the alley every evening.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: وكل صيف كنا كنمشيو عند جدي فالبادية.
dialogue.transliteration: w kol Seef kunna kanmshiw 3and jeddi f-l-baadiya.
dialogue.english: And every summer we went to my grandfather's in the countryside.

dialogue.speaker: Kareem
dialogue.arabic: وجدتك كانت كتحكي لكم حكايات؟
dialogue.transliteration: w jeddtek kant kat7ki lkum 7kaayaat?
dialogue.english: And did your grandmother tell you stories?

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: إيه، قبل ما ننعسو. وكنت كنخاف من الضلمة!
dialogue.transliteration: eeh, qbel ma nn3essu. w kunt kankhaaf mn D-Dlma!
dialogue.english: Yes, before we slept. And I was afraid of the dark!

dialogue.speaker: Kareem
dialogue.arabic: أنا كنت كنحلم نولي طيار.
dialogue.transliteration: ana kunt kan7lem nwelli Tayyaar.
dialogue.english: I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: والمعلم ديالنا كان حنين بزاف معانا.
dialogue.transliteration: w l-m3allem dyaalna kan 7neen bzzaf m3aana.
dialogue.english: And our teacher was very kind to us.

dialogue.speaker: Kareem
dialogue.arabic: وكنا كنمشيو للمدرسة مع بعضنا كل نهار.
dialogue.transliteration: w kunna kanmshiw l-l-medrasa m3a b3Dna kol nhar.
dialogue.english: And we walked to school together every day.

dialogue.speaker: Hind
dialogue.arabic: فديك الساعة الدنيا كانت ساهلة بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: f-deek s-saa3a d-dunya kant saahla bzzaf.
dialogue.english: Back then life was much simpler.

response.english: In an old neighbourhood in Casablanca.

pair.english: What did you play in the alley?
What did you dream of becoming?

response.english: I dreamed of becoming a pilot.

pair.english: How did you go to school?

lessons.culture: Many Casablanca and Rabat families still have roots in the countryside, so summers at the grandparents' house in the البادية (or the بلاد, as people also say) are a familiar childhood memory. Playing football in the درب, the neighbourhood alley, is just as typical.

exercises.prompt: كيسولوك: "شكون كان صاحبك فالدرب؟". جاوب بلي كان عندك صاحب سميتو كريم.

too_formal.feedback: Correct MSA, but too bookish for everyday Darija; كان عندي and سميتو are what is said.

exercises.prompt: كيسولوك: "شنو كنتو كتديرو فالصيف؟". جاوب بلي كنتو كتمشيو عند جدك فالبادية.

too_formal.item: كنا نذهب إلى جدي في القرية
too_formal.feedback: The Darija habit form is كنا كنمشيو, not نذهب.

exercises.tip: "كنمشيو" = we go; with "كنا" it means we used to go.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "ملي كنت _____ كنت كنبغي نلعب برا." المعنى: When I was young I loved to play outside.

too_formal.feedback: طفلا is bookish; ملي كنت صغير is the natural way.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "كنا كنلعبو _____ فالدرب." المعنى: We used to play football in the alley.

too_formal.feedback: كرة القدم is the formal name; people say الكورة.

exercises.tip: "الكورة" is the ball and the game of football.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "When I was young I dreamed of becoming a pilot."
exercises.answer: مْلِي كُنْتْ صْغِيرْ كُنْتْ كْنْحلِمْ نْوَلِّي طيَّارْ
accepted: مْلِي كُنْتْ صْغِيرْ كُنْتْ كْنْحلِمْ نْوَلِّي طيَّارْ
mli kunt Sgheer kunt kan7lem nwelli Tayyaar
كنت كنحلم نولي طيار ملي كنت صغير

too_formal.item: عندما كنت صغيرا كنت أحلم أن أصبح طيارا
too_formal.feedback: Spoken Darija uses ملي, كنحلم and نولي.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Back then life was much simpler."
exercises.answer: فْدِيكْ السَّاعَة الدُّنْيَا كَانَتْ سَاهْلَة بزَّافْ
accepted: فْدِيكْ السَّاعَة الدُّنْيَا كَانَتْ سَاهْلَة بزَّافْ
f-deek s-saa3a d-dunya kant saahla bzzaf

too_formal.item: في ذلك الوقت كانت الحياة أبسط بكثير
too_formal.feedback: Bookish; the spoken word for life here is الدنيا and for very is بزاف.

exercises.prompt: شنو معنى "كنا كنمشيو للمدرسة مع بعضنا كل نهار"؟
exercises.answer: We used to walk to school together every day.
accepted: We used to walk to school together every day.
options: We used to walk to school together every day.
We will go to school tomorrow.
We went to school by bus.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "My grandmother used to tell us stories before sleeping"؟
exercises.answer: جَدِّتِي كَانَتْ كْتْحكِي لِينَا حْكَايَاتْ قْبَلْ مَا ننْعِسُّو
accepted: جَدِّتِي كَانَتْ كْتْحكِي لِينَا حْكَايَاتْ قْبَلْ مَا ننْعِسُّو
jeddti kant kat7ki leena 7kaayaat qbel ma nn3essu
options: جَدِّتِي كَانَتْ كْتْحكِي لِينَا حْكَايَاتْ قْبَلْ مَا ننْعِسُّو

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: المعلم ديالي فالمدرسة كان حنين بزاف
exercises.answer: الْمُعَلِّمْ دِيَالِي فَالْمدْرَسَة كَانْ حْنِينْ بزَّافْ
accepted: الْمُعَلِّمْ دِيَالِي فَالْمدْرَسَة كَانْ حْنِينْ بزَّافْ

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: جدتي كانت كتحكي لينا حكايات قبل ما ننعسو
exercises.answer: جَدِّتِي كَانَتْ كْتْحكِي لِينَا حْكَايَاتْ قْبَلْ مَا ننْعِسُّو
accepted: جَدِّتِي كَانَتْ كْتْحكِي لِينَا حْكَايَاتْ قْبَلْ مَا ننْعِسُّو

phrases.transliteration: Tu7t f-d-drooj w t3awrat lia rejli

phrases.arabic: تْكبَّاتْ لِيَا الْقهْوَة عْلَى الْكمْبِيُوتِرْ دِيَالِي

phrases.transliteration: tqTe3at lia yeddi w ana kanTeyyeb

phrases.arabic: غلَطْتْ وْصِيفْطِتْ الْمِيسَاجْ لْشِي وَاحِدْ آخِرْ
phrases.transliteration: ghleTt w SeefeTt l-messaj l-shi waa7ed aakhor
n3est bzzaf w ma sme3tsh l-menabbeh

dialogue.speaker: Mehdi
dialogue.arabic: خديجة، فين كنتي؟ تعطلتي على الخدمة؟
dialogue.transliteration: Khadija, fin knti? t3aTTelti 3la l-khedma?
dialogue.english: Khadija, where were you? Were you late for work?

dialogue.speaker: Khadija
dialogue.arabic: أوه، ما تسول ليش! تكسر ليا التيليفون البارح.
dialogue.transliteration: oh, ma tsool leesh! tkesser lia t-telefon l-baare7.
dialogue.english: Oh, don't ask! My phone broke yesterday.

dialogue.speaker: Mehdi
dialogue.arabic: الله يعوض. وشنو وقع ليك أكثر؟
dialogue.transliteration: Allah y3awweD. w shnu wq3 leek ktar?
dialogue.english: May God compensate you. And what else happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Khadija
dialogue.arabic: طحت فالدروج وتعورات ليا رجلي.
dialogue.transliteration: Tu7t f-d-drooj w t3awrat lia rejli.
dialogue.english: I fell on the stairs and hurt my leg.

dialogue.speaker: Mehdi
dialogue.arabic: سلامتك! واش كتوجعك بزاف؟
dialogue.transliteration: slaamtek! waash katwj3ek bzzaf?
dialogue.english: Get well soon! Does it hurt a lot?

dialogue.speaker: Khadija
dialogue.arabic: شوية. وزيد على هادشي، ضاع ليا السروت د الدار.
dialogue.transliteration: shwiya. w zeed 3la haadshi, Daa3 lia s-sarut d d-daar.
dialogue.english: A little. And on top of that I lost the house key.

dialogue.speaker: Mehdi
dialogue.arabic: وكيفاش دخلتي للدار؟
dialogue.transliteration: w keefaash dkhelti l-d-daar?
dialogue.english: And how did you get into the house?

dialogue.speaker: Khadija
dialogue.arabic: ختي كانت فالدار، الحمد لله.
dialogue.transliteration: khti kant f-d-daar, l-7amdulillah.
dialogue.english: My sister was at home, thank God.

dialogue.speaker: Mehdi
dialogue.arabic: وأنا البارح الضو مشا طول الليل.
dialogue.transliteration: w ana l-baare7 D-Dew msha Tool l-leel.
dialogue.english: And yesterday my power went out all night.

dialogue.speaker: Khadija
dialogue.arabic: يا ربي! وأنا تكبات ليا القهوة على الكمبيوتر.
dialogue.transliteration: yaa rebbi! w ana tkebbat lia l-qahwa 3la l-kompyutur.
dialogue.english: Oh Lord! And coffee spilled on my laptop.

dialogue.speaker: Mehdi
dialogue.arabic: الله يستر! هاد الأسبوع ما فيه غير المشاكل.
dialogue.transliteration: Allah ysster! haad l-osbo3 ma fih ghir l-mashaakil.
dialogue.english: May God protect us! This week is nothing but problems.

dialogue.speaker: Khadija
dialogue.arabic: مرة مرة كيوقع هكا. الله يعوض.
dialogue.transliteration: merra merra kiwqa3 hakka. Allah y3awweD.
dialogue.english: It happens like that sometimes. May God compensate.

pair.english: Why were you late for work?

response.english: The car broke down in the middle of the road.
Yes, I forgot my wallet at home.

lessons.culture: When someone tells you their bad luck, the usual answers are الله يعوض (may God compensate you) and, for an injury, سلامتك. Moroccans also add الحمد لله على كل حال even when things went wrong.

exercises.prompt: واحد كيقول ليك: "تكسر ليا التيليفون". جاوبو.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but stiff; الله يعوض is what people say.

exercises.tip: "الله يعوض" is the standard answer to a loss.

exercises.prompt: واحد كيقول ليك: "طحت فالدروج وتعورات ليا رجلي". قول ليه "get well soon".

too_formal.feedback: Not said in speech; سلامتك is the everyday wish.

exercises.tip: "سلامتك" is said to someone who is hurt or ill.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "_____ ليا التيليفون البارح." المعنى: My phone broke yesterday.

too_formal.feedback: انكسر is Levantine and MSA; in Morocco it is تكسر.

exercises.tip: "تكسر" is the reflexive form: it broke on its own.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "نسيت _____ ديالي فالدار." المعنى: I forgot my wallet at home.

too_formal.feedback: المحفظة is MSA; the everyday word is البورطوفوي.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "I lost the house key."

too_formal.feedback: Darija says ضاع ليا and السروت for a key.

exercises.tip: "ضاع ليا" = it got lost on me.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "The car broke down in the middle of the road."

too_formal.feedback: السيارة and منتصف are formal; الطونوبيل and وسط are spoken.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "The power went out all night"؟
شنو معنى "نعست بزاف وما سمعتش المنبه"؟
exercises.answer: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.
accepted: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.
options: I overslept and didn't hear the alarm.
I woke up early and left.
I heard the alarm but stayed in bed.
I forgot my phone at home.
exercises.tip: "ما ... ش" wraps a verb to make it negative.

exercises.prompt: رتب الجملة: طحت فالدروج وتعورات ليا رجلي
رتب الجملة: ضاعت ليا الشنطة فالمطار
exercises.tip: "الشنطة" = the bag; a feminine noun, so ضاعت.

phrases.english: I heard that Samir got engaged.

phrases.arabic: عِنْدِي لِيكْ خبِرْ مَا غَادِيشْ تصِدْقُو
قَالُو لِيَا بْلِي غَادِي تْبدِّلْ الدَّارْ
phrases.transliteration: qaalu lia bli ghaadi tbeddel d-daar

phrases.arabic: مَازَالْ مَا مْتأَكِّدِينْشْ، يمْكِنْ غِيرْ إشَاعَة
phrases.transliteration: maazal ma mt2akdeensh, yemken ghir ishaa3a

phrases.arabic: مَا غَادِيشْ تصِدِّقْ شنُو وْقعِ الْبَارِحْ فَالْحُومَة
phrases.transliteration: ma ghaadish tSeddeq shnu wq3 l-baare7 f-l-7uma

phrases.arabic: مَا تْقُولْشْ لْحدِّ، وْلَاكِينْ سْمِعْتْ بْلِي غَادِي يْسَافْرُو
phrases.transliteration: ma tqulsh l-7ed, walaakin sme3t bli ghaadi ysaafru

phrases.arabic: هَادْشِي غِيرْ هدْرَة د النَّاسْ، مَا عرِفْتْشْ وَاشْ صحِيحْ وْلَا لَا
phrases.transliteration: haadshi ghir hedra d n-naas, ma 3reftsh waash Se7ee7 wla la

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: يوسف، عندي ليك خبر ما غاديش تصدقو!
dialogue.transliteration: Youssef, 3endi leek khbar ma ghaadish tSeddqu!
dialogue.english: Youssef, I have news you won't believe!

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: شنو؟ قولي ليا!
dialogue.transliteration: shnu? qooli lia!
dialogue.english: What? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: سمعت بلي سمير خطب.
dialogue.transliteration: sme3t bli Sameer khTeb.
dialogue.english: I heard that Sameer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: بصح؟ شكون قال ليك؟
dialogue.transliteration: bS-S7? shkoon qaal leek?
dialogue.english: Really? Who told you?

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: صاحبتي قالت ليا، ولاكين مازال ما متأكدينش.
dialogue.transliteration: Saa7abti qaalat lia, walaakin maazal ma mt2akdeensh.
dialogue.english: My friend told me, but we are not sure yet.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: يمكن غير إشاعة. الناس كيهضرو بزاف.
dialogue.transliteration: yemken ghir ishaa3a. n-naas kihderru bzzaf.
dialogue.english: Maybe it is just a rumour. People talk a lot.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: يمكن. وشنو الجديد عندك؟
dialogue.transliteration: yemken. w shnu l-jdeed 3endek?
dialogue.english: Maybe. And what is new with you?

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: والو، ختي تزوجات الشهر الفايت.
dialogue.transliteration: waalu, khti tzewjat sh-shhar l-faayt.
dialogue.english: Nothing, my sister got married last month.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: مبروك عليها! الله يبارك ليها.
dialogue.transliteration: mabruk 3liha! Allah ybaarek liha.
dialogue.english: Congratulations to her! May God bless her.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: الله يبارك فيك. وسمعنا بلي تزاد ليهم ولد.
dialogue.transliteration: Allah ybaarek fiik. w sme3na bli tzaad lihum weld.
dialogue.english: May God bless you. And we heard they had a baby boy.

dialogue.speaker: Salma
dialogue.arabic: ما تقولش لحد، ولاكين سمعت بلي غادي يسافرو.
dialogue.transliteration: ma tqulsh l-7ed, walaakin sme3t bli ghaadi ysaafru.
dialogue.english: Don't tell anyone, but I heard they are going to travel.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: هادشي غير هدرة د الناس، ما عرفتش واش صحيح ولا لا.
dialogue.transliteration: haadshi ghir hedra d n-naas, ma 3reftsh waash Se7ee7 wla la.
dialogue.english: That is just people's talk, I don't know if it is true or not.

response.english: I don't know, it might be a rumour.

lessons.culture: Congratulations on an engagement, wedding or birth are مبروك followed by الله يبارك ليه or ليها. Moroccans often hedge gossip with يمكن or كيقولو and end with الله أعلم, since repeating what is not certain is frowned on.

exercises.prompt: واحد كيقول ليك: "ختي تزوجات الشهر الفايت". جاوبو.

too_formal.feedback: Correct but formal; مبروك عليها is the everyday response.

exercises.tip: Add الله يبارك ليها for a fuller blessing.

exercises.prompt: كيسولوك: "شنو الجديد عندك؟". جاوب بلي والو، غير الخدمة والدار.

too_formal.feedback: Bookish; والو and غير are the spoken words.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "سمعت _____ سمير خطب." المعنى: I heard that Sameer got engaged.

too_formal.feedback: أن is MSA; Darija uses بلي.

exercises.prompt: كمل: "هادشي غير _____ د الناس." المعنى: That is just people's talk.

too_formal.feedback: كلام is understood, but هدرة is the Moroccan word for talk.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "Who told you this news?"

too_formal.feedback: Formal; شكون قال ليك is what is said.

exercises.prompt: ترجم: "My sister got married last month."

too_formal.feedback: الماضي is MSA; الفايت is the spoken word.

exercises.prompt: أي جملة معناها "They're saying that such-and-such shop closed"؟
شنو معنى "ما تقولش لحد"؟
رتب الجملة: سمعنا بلي تزاد ليهم ولد
رتب الجملة: مازال ما متأكدينش يمكن غير إشاعة
exercises.answer: مازال ما متأكدينش يمكن غير إشاعة
accepted: مازال ما متأكدينش يمكن غير إشاعة

challenge.title: قول ليا شنو وقع
challenge.instructions: Write and say a short Darija conversation of at least 10 lines between two people catching up. It must include asking what happened yesterday, an answer in the past tense, a childhood memory, one thing that went wrong, and one piece of news or gossip you heard. Use at least 8 target phrases from Unit 16 and include both a masculine-address form and a feminine-address form.
required_elements: A question about yesterday using البارح and شنو درتي.
An answer describing something that happened, using a past-tense verb.
A memory from childhood using ملي كنت صغير or كنا.
Something that went wrong, using a word like تكسر, ضاع, or تعطلت.
A piece of news or gossip introduced with سمعت بلي or قالو ليا.
At least one address to a woman, using a form such as شفتي or كنتي.
At least one address to a man by name, and one feminine self-reference such as ملي كنت صغيرة.
A closing reaction such as الله يعوض, يا ربي, or الله يستر.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: ميساء، كيداير؟ شنو درتي البارح؟
dialogue.transliteration: Maysaa2, keedaayer? shnu derti l-baare7?
dialogue.english: Maysa, how are you? What did you do yesterday?

dialogue.speaker: Maysa
dialogue.arabic: أهلا بلال، ما غاديش تصدق شنو وقع ليا البارح!
dialogue.transliteration: ahlan Bilaal, ma ghaadish tSeddeq shnu wq3 lia l-baare7!
dialogue.english: Hi Bilal, you won't believe what happened to me yesterday!

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: شنو وقع؟ قولي ليا!
dialogue.transliteration: shnu wq3? qooli lia!
dialogue.english: What happened? Tell me!

dialogue.speaker: Maysa
dialogue.arabic: تكسر ليا التيليفون وضاع ليا السروت د الدار فنفس النهار.
dialogue.transliteration: tkesser lia t-telefon w Daa3 lia s-sarut d d-daar f-nefs n-nhar.
dialogue.english: My phone broke and I lost the house key on the same day.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: يا ربي! هاد النهار كيفكرني ملي كنا صغار، كنا كنضيعو كلشي!
dialogue.transliteration: yaa rebbi! haad n-nhar kifekkerni mli kunna Sghaar, kunna kanDee3u kolshi!
dialogue.english: Oh Lord! A day like that reminds me of when we were small, we used to lose everything!

dialogue.speaker: Maysa
dialogue.arabic: هاهاها صح! ولاكين لقيت السروت فالأخير.
dialogue.transliteration: hahaha S-S7! walaakin lqit s-sarut f-l-akheer.
dialogue.english: Haha true! But I found the key in the end.

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: الحمد لله. وبالمناسبة، سمعت بلي سمير خطب.
dialogue.transliteration: l-7amdulillah. w b-l-munaasaba, sme3t bli Sameer khTeb.
dialogue.english: Thank God. By the way, I heard Sameer got engaged.

dialogue.speaker: Maysa
dialogue.arabic: لا! بصح؟ شكون قال ليك؟
dialogue.transliteration: la! bS-S7? shkoon qaal leek?
dialogue.english: No! Really? Who told you?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: صاحبتي قالت ليا، ولاكين مازال ما متأكدينش.
dialogue.transliteration: Saa7abti qaalat lia, walaakin maazal ma mt2akdeensh.
dialogue.english: My friend told me, but we are not sure yet.

dialogue.speaker: Maysa
dialogue.arabic: الله يبارك إلا كان صحيح. وانت شفتي كيفاش داز ليك نهار؟
dialogue.transliteration: Allah ybaarek ila kan S7ee7. w nta shefti keefaash daaz leek nhaar?
dialogue.english: God bless if it is true. And you, did you see how your day went?

dialogue.speaker: Bilal
dialogue.arabic: هاديك هي الدنيا، نهار حلو ونهار خايب.
dialogue.transliteration: haadik hiya d-dunya, nhaar 7lu w nhaar khaayeb.
dialogue.english: That is life, a good day and a bad day.
